text:
The Islanders and Sharks meet in San Jose with both teams looking for a way out of a skid. NYI is winless in three (0-2-1) after Saturday's 5-4 overtime loss to New Jersey, a game the Devils won after trailing by two goals. San Jose is winless in five (0-5-0), outscored 22-8 over that stretch, and it is leaning on Macklin Celebrini. As Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest posted, the Sharks "can't play Macklin Celebrini 28 minutes every night, but they have to right now."

Our numbers say neither team has been getting the better of the chances, but San Jose has had it worse. Over the last five games the Sharks have taken 40% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and the Islanders 46%. NYI's power play and penalty kill both rate better, though it takes 4.7 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Ilya Sorokin (+6.1 goals saved above expected this season, +22.3 last year) and Yaroslav Askarov (+4.4 this season, -19.4 last year) give New York the clearer edge. We have the model at 3.35 expected goals for NYI and 3.08 for SJS.

Celebrini is our top pick at 44% to score and 84% for a point, one short of 200 career points. Will Smith is one goal from 50. Bo Horvat leads NYI at 41% to score. Without Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie, Simon Holmstrom has moved onto the first power-play unit and is up to 20:44 a night from 15:43. We like him as an under-the-radar pick at 52% for a point, as the Sharks give up the most expected goals per 60. We'd also watch Sharks third-liner Ivar Stenberg, whose shots have been dangerous lately. He's at 22% to score.
